TICKETME.need: the relationship to the VALIDATION seal already in the tester, which is the existing measured-green artifact and the obvious place to derive from rather than build beside (Law 1).

marks.need: the relationship to the VALIDATION seal already in the tester, which is the existing measured-green artifact and the obvious place to derive from rather than build beside (Law 1).
marks.how_measured: Akien's ruling: 'Green is a state at a point in time. A certificate is the unforgeable proof.' The validation seal IS the certificate. Green is derived from what was true at issuance — not a live meter. The seal's relationship is: it is the proof artifact; green is the state that was certified. Decision 2026-08-20-green-yellow-red-proportional-to-the-thing.

BUILDME.need: derive red/yellow/green per component from: (a) certificate existence and validity, (b) own-code change since last certificate → red, (c) dependency change only → yellow, (d) operational logs showing continued function → self-cleaning yellow→green through the gate
the site-plan surface that shows unbuilt lots — components declared in the intentions but with no code, no charter, no certificate. The whole site starts red.

proportionality: simple components (basic sieves) do not need re-review when neighbors change as long as they keep operating correctly. The mechanism must not demand uniform observability from every component.

[CLOSED 2026-08-20] WHERE DOES THE SITE PLAN GET THE UNBUILT LOTS? ANSWERED by the three-state ruling: the intentions declare the whole; a component with no code, no charter, no certificate is red by default (the whole site starts red). The site plan reads from the intentions-not-beside-code folder plus the charters beside code — what has no certificate is red, what has never been started is the reddest. The 'unbuilt lot' is any intention without a corresponding proved component.
